pNone_chapter_1: In a sunlit colonial-style living room in Kolkata, Byomkesh Bakshi sits in a wooden armchair, leaning forward with a contemplative expression while holding a lit cigarette. Ajit stands near a mahogany side table, holding a black rotary telephone to his ear with a look of focused attention. A morning newspaper lies unfolded on a small tea table between them, its pages catching the bright morning light streaming through slatted windows. Both men are dressed in traditional white pleated dhotis and kurtas, their silhouettes sharp against the backdrop of a bookshelf-lined wall.
